title: The Reference Request Note
subtitle: Before you ask a customer to help with a deal
intro_text: Use this with the account owner before approaching the customer. Keep the answer in the existing opportunity notes. Do not add customer names to this public copy.

example.heading: Example: a prospect asks about rollout
example.label: Fictional example, not a customer result.
example.interpretation: The story may not answer the whole question. The customer gets a specific, optional request rather than a demand for a call tomorrow.

sections.title: What question needs answering?
sections.instruction: Write the buyer's actual question. Why is this customer the right person to answer it?

sections.title: What would we ask the customer to give?
sections.instruction: State the format, time, audience and deadline. Check prior asks and the exact permission needed. Include the customer's possible benefit without dressing up a favour as a benefit.

sections.title: Is there a smaller way?
sections.instruction: Choose: ask as planned, make a smaller ask, use existing proof, or wait. Name the person who will ask and the next step if the customer declines.

prompt:
Buyer question: [ ]
Exact customer ask: [format, audience, time, deadline]
Why this customer: [ ]
Permission and recent asks checked: [ ]
Smaller option: [ ]
Decision and owner: [ ]
next_action: Use on one live request. The customer's no must remain a real option. Follow your company's permission process for names, quotes and logos.
methodology: An editorial decision aid, not a proven way to improve sales or retention. The sources and limits are in the article.
